τύραννος / τύραννοι (Wisdom of Solomon 6:9, 21; 8:15; 12:14; 14:16, 21)

absolute ruler(s) in every verse (6:9 'you absolute rulers', 6:21 'you absolute rulers of peoples'), never 'tyrants' in Wisdom, since the address is to rulers the book hopes to win; a note at 6:9. Other books keep 'tyrant' where the story shows cruelty (2 Maccabees 4:25; 7:27). Lead decision 11 (2026-10-31). Added by Wis 06-10.
πνευμάτων βίας (Wisdom of Solomon 7:20)
'the force of the winds', with a note giving 'spirits'; adds 7:20 to the 'wind' uses in the πνεῦμα (Wisdom of Solomon) entry. Added by Wis 06-10.
ὁ μέγιστος θεός (3 Maccabees 1:16; 3:11 and often)
the Most Great God (one rendering everywhere; note at 1:16; at 1:9 Codex Alexandrinus has 'the faithful God', a variant). Added by 3Ma 01-03.
ἱερόν / ναός (3 Maccabees 1:9-2:24; 3:16-17)
the temple (the whole complex) / the sanctuary (the holy house, here the Most Holy Place the king wants to enter), kept apart as in the Gospels; note at 1:10. Added by 3Ma 01-03.
λαογραφία / ἀπογράφομαι, ἀπογραφή (3 Maccabees 2:28-32)
the census, the census rolls (a list of people for taxes) / be registered, enrolled / the registration; note at 2:28. Added by 3Ma 01-03.
ἰσοπολῖται / πολιτεία, of Alexandrian status (3 Maccabees 2:30; 3:21, 23)
equal citizens / citizenship (in 3 Maccabees the civic sense, not 2 Maccabees' 'way of life'); notes at 2:30 and 3:21. Added by 3Ma 01-03.
εὐσέβεια / δυσσεβής (3 Maccabees)
godliness / impious (as 2 Maccabees for δυσσεβής). Added by 3Ma 01-03.
φίλοι, the court rank (3 Maccabees 2:23, 26; 5:29; 6:23)
Friends (capitalized, as in 1 and 2 Maccabees). Added by 3Ma 01-03.
πνεῦμα δυνάμεως (Wisdom of Solomon 5:23; 11:20)
'a wind of power' at 5:23 (it 'blows them away like a whirlwind'), with a note giving 'Spirit of power'; adds 5:23 to the 'wind' uses in the πνεῦμα (Wisdom of Solomon) entry. Added by Wis 01-05.
παῖς Κυρίου (Wisdom of Solomon 2:13)

'child of the Lord' (the Greek has Κυρίου, not θεοῦ, so not 'child of God' as the brief had it), with a note on 'servant/child' and Isaiah 52:13 (Greek ὁ παῖς μου); υἱὸς θεοῦ at 2:18 'God's son'. Added by Wis 01-05.
ἀρετή (Wisdom of Solomon 4:1; 5:13; 8:7)
virtue. Added by Wis 01-05.
ὑπερισχύω / ἰσχυρός (1 Esdras 3-4)
is strongest / strong (one English verb for the key word of the contest: 3:5, 10-12, 17, 23; 4:2-3, 12, 41; the cry of 4:41 is "Great is truth, and it is strongest!")
ἀλήθεια (1 Esdras)
truth (one English word in every verse of 3:12 and 4:33-41, and at 5:40, where τὴν δήλωσιν καὶ τὴν ἀλήθειαν, the Greek for the Urim and Thummim, is "the Showing and the Truth")
συγγενής, as a court title (1 Esdras 3:7; 4:42)
Kinsman (capitalized, as in 1 Maccabees 10:89; 11:31)
ἱερόδουλοι (1 Esdras 5:29, 35)
temple servants (as netinim in Ezra 2:43; the note gives the Greek sense 'temple slaves')
ἱεροψάλται (1 Esdras)
temple singers (Ezra's meshorerim 'singers'; note at 5:27)
ὁ αἰώνιος, as a name of God (Baruch 4:10, 4:14, 4:20, 4:22 twice, 4:24, 4:35; 5:2)
the Everlasting (capital E, the same rendering everywhere, with a note at Baruch 4:10); θεὸς αἰώνιος (Baruch 4:8) 'the everlasting God'. Added by Bar 01-05. Count corrected by the Bar 01-05 review.
ὁ ἅγιος, as a name of God (Baruch 4:22, 4:37; 5:5)
the Holy One. Added by Bar 01-05.
σοφία / φρόνησις / ἐπιστήμη / σύνεσις (Baruch 3:9–4:4)
wisdom / insight / understanding / discernment (one English word for each, kept apart; note at Baruch 3:9). Added by Bar 01-05.
πρόσταγμα / ἐντολή / δικαίωμα (Baruch 1–5)

commands / commandments / rulings (δικαιώματα 'righteous deeds' where people's deeds are meant, Baruch 2:19; δικαίωμα 'justice' where it is given to God beside 'glory', Baruch 2:17); ἡ βίβλος τῶν προσταγμάτων τοῦ θεοῦ (Baruch 4:1) 'the book of the commands of God'. Added by Bar 01-05.
θαρσεῖτε / θαρρεῖτε / θαρρήσατε / θάρσει (Baruch 4:5, 4:21, 4:27, 4:30)
Take heart (the refrain that opens each stanza of the consolation). Added by Bar 01-05.
μάννα for Hebrew minchah (Baruch 1:10; Greek Jeremiah 17:26; 48:5)
grain offering(s), with a note that the Greek writes the Hebrew word in Greek letters (KJV 'manna'). Added by Bar 01-05.
θεοί / εἴδωλα (Letter of Jeremiah, Baruch 6)

'gods' for θεοί in every verse of the Letter (6:3–71), including the refrain 'they are not gods'; 'idols' only for εἴδωλα (6:72, its one use). Why: the brief proposed 'gods' only in Babylonian speech and 'idols' otherwise, but the Letter's argument is that the statues cannot be called gods (6:39, 6:44, 6:56, 6:63), which 'they are not idols' would empty; lead decision 2026-10-31. Note at Baruch 6:4. Added by Bar 06-06 (review fix).
τεχνῖτις σοφία (Wisdom of Solomon 14:2)

'Wisdom, the craftswoman', with a capital W, as 'Wisdom, who crafted all things' at 7:22; replaces "τεχνῖτις σοφία (14:2) 'a craftsman's wisdom'" in the σοφία (Wisdom of Solomon) entry of content/terms.json. Why: lead decision 8 (one rule for all parts: capital W where she acts or is described as a person, including the feminine epithet τεχνῖτις). Note at 14:2. Added by Wis 11-15 fix.
παιδεία / παιδεύω (Sirach 1:0–6:37)

discipline by default (1:27; 4:17), 'instruction' / 'be instructed' where the sense is teaching and learning (prologue; 4:24; 6:18; 6:32; the Latin line 1:7), with a note at the prologue; ἀπαίδευτοι 'the undisciplined' where the context is correction (6:20); ἀπαιδευσία 'how little you have been taught' (4:25, schooling), following the lead's rule for all Sirach parts (51:23 'untaught'). Added by Sir 01-06.
σοφία (Sirach)
wisdom; 'Wisdom' with a capital where she acts as a person (1:4; 1:6; 4:11–19; 6:22, and her pronouns in 1:9–20 and 6:18–31), as in the Wisdom of Solomon entry. Added by Sir 01-06.
τέκνον / τέκνα (Sirach)
my child / children (Hebrew בני 'my son' where it survives; note at 2:1). Added by Sir 01-06.
ἐξιλάσκομαι / ἐξιλασμός (Sirach 3:3, 30; 5:5–6)
make atonement for / atone for; atonement (as kipper 'make atonement'). Added by Sir 01-06.
ἐλεημοσύνη (Sirach 3:14, 30)

alms at 3:30 (gloss 'gifts to the poor', as the shared entry); 'mercy shown to a father' at 3:14, where it is kindness to a parent; the Hebrew has tsedaqah both times (notes); a gloss at 3:14 says the Greek word is the one for alms. Added by Sir 01-06.
δίγλωσσος (Sirach 5:9, 14; 6:1)

the sinner who has two tongues (refrain 'That is how it is with the sinner who has two tongues', 5:9; 6:1); 'the man with two tongues' (5:14); Hebrew ba'al shtayim 'two-faced' in a note. Added by Sir 01-06.
φίλος πιστός (Sirach 6:14–16)
a faithful friend (the same English each time). Added by Sir 01-06.
οἱ φοβούμενοι (τὸν) Κύριον (Sirach 2:7–9, 15–17)
'you who fear the Lord' (the vocative refrain, placed at the end of the first line) / 'those who fear the Lord'. Added by Sir 01-06.
ὀκνηρός (Sirach 22:1-2; the Greek of Proverbs 6:6)
the lazy one (Proverbs' rendering of 'atsel, whose Greek uses this word; never 'sluggard'). Added by Sir 19-23.
πανοῦργος / πανουργία (Sirach 19:25; 21:12, 20; 22:27)
shrewd / shrewdness, in the good and the bad sense alike, as Proverbs 14:15 'a shrewd person' (Greek πανοῦργος); note at Sirach 21:12. Added by Sir 19-23.
φρόνιμος / φρόνησις / συνετός / ἀσύνετος / νοήμων (Sirach)
sensible (as the Gospels entry for φρόνιμος) / good sense / a person of understanding / a person without understanding / thoughtful. Added by Sir 19-23.
παιδεία / παιδεύω / ἀπαίδευτος / ἀπαιδευσία / πεπαιδευμένος (Sirach 19-23)

one rule for all of Sirach (lead decision 6, 2026-10-31): παιδεία 'discipline' by default, 'instruction' (παιδεύω 'teach') where the sense is teaching, with a note at the first use in each part; ἀπαίδευτος 'undisciplined' where the context is correction, 'untaught' where it is schooling (6:20; 51:23). In 19-23: 'discipline' at 19:19; 21:19, 21; 22:6; 23:2, 7, 15; 'undisciplined' at 20:19, 24; 22:3 (the whip is close by: 22:6; 23:2); 'lack of discipline' at 21:24; 22:10; 23:13; 'disciplined' at 21:23; 'cannot be taught' at 21:12 (schooling). Note at Sirach 20:19. Added by Sir 19-23, reconciled to decision 6.
ἐλέγχω (Sirach 19:13-17); ἔλεγχος / ἐλεγμός
take it up with (the fourfold command of 19:13-17, where the friend may be innocent; note at 19:13 on Leviticus 19:17 and Matthew 18:15) / rebuke (20:1-2) / correction (21:6). Added by Sir 19-23.
σκηνή / κατασκηνόω (Sirach 24:4, 8, 10, 15; 28:16)

tent / pitch a tent (the same English each time, so the thread to John 1:14 'pitched his tent among us' shows; a note gives 'tabernacle' where the sanctuary is meant, as in the Hebrews entry). Added by Sir 24-29.
γυνὴ ἀνδρεία / γυναῖκες ἀνδρεῖαι (Sirach 26:2; 28:15)
a wife of strength / wives of strength (Manuscript C has eshet chayil at 26:2, the phrase of Proverbs 31:10 'A woman of strength'). Added by Sir 24-29.
ἐγγυάω / ἔγγυος / ἐγγύη (Sirach 29:14–19)
stand good for / guarantor / standing good for others (as the Proverbs 'arav entry; Hebrews 7:22 uses ἔγγυος of Jesus). Added by Sir 24-29.
μακάριος (Sirach)
happy (as ashrei, 'Happy is the one who'; 25:7–9; 26:1; 28:19). Added by Sir 24-29.
γλῶσσα τρίτη (Sirach 28:14–15)
the tongue of a third party (probably a Hebrew idiom for slander; no Hebrew of chapter 28 survives; note at 28:14 with Arakhin 15b). Added by Sir 24-29.
πάροικος / παροικέω (Sirach 29:24–27)
lodger / lodge as a stranger (a man with no house of his own who lives on others; the note at 29:24 gives the Ephesians entry's 'resident alien'). Added by Sir 24-29.
ποδήρης (Sirach 27:8)
an ankle-length robe (as Wisdom of Solomon 18:24). Added by Sir 24-29.
κληρονομία / κατακληρονομέω (Sirach 24:7–23)

inheritance / take up an inheritance, the same English each time, also at 24:23, where the line takes up Deuteronomy 33:4: the Plain keeps the Greek's word, and the note there says that Deuteronomy's Plain has 'heritage' because it renders the Hebrew morashah (lead decision 9). Added by Sir 24-29.
βδέλυγμα (Sirach 27:30)
something abhorrent; 'abhorrent things' for the plural at 27:30 (lead decision 13; as to'evah). Added by Sir 24-29.
παιδεία / πεπαιδευμένη (Sirach 24-29)
under the one Sirach rule (lead decision 6): 'instruction' at 24:27 and 24:32, where the sense is teaching (note at 24:32), and 'well-instructed' for πεπαιδευμένη at 26:14. Added by Sir 24-29.
διαβούλιον (Sirach 15:14; 17:6)
choice ('left him in the hand of his own choice', 15:14; 'He gave them choice, a tongue and eyes', 17:6); the Hebrew of 15:14 has yetser 'inclination' (note there). Added by Sir 13-18.
βάσκανος / βασκαίνω / ὀφθαλμὸς πονηρός (Sirach 14:3-10; 18:18)
grudging (a grudging man; begrudge) / an evil eye, as Proverbs 23:6 'a man with a grudging eye' for ra' ayin and Matthew 20:15 'is your eye evil'; note at Sirach 14:3. Added by Sir 13-18.
βδέλυγμα (Sirach 13:20; 15:13; 17:26)
abhorrent / everything abhorrent / the abhorrent thing, as the shared to'evah entry (the Hebrew of 13:20 and 15:13 has to'evah). Added by Sir 13-18.
ἐξιλάσκομαι / ἐξιλασμός with God as the one who acts (Sirach 16:7, 11; 17:29; 18:12, 20)

make atonement / atonement, as the Sir 01-06 entry, also where God is the one who wipes sin away: 'He made no atonement for the giants of long ago' (16:7), 'mighty in atonement' (16:11, Greek dynastēs exilasmōn), 'the atonement he gives those who turn back to him' (17:29); notes at 16:7 and 16:11 give the Hebrew 'did not forgive' and 'bears and pardons'. Added by Sir 13-18.
μακάριος (Sirach 14:1-2, 20)
Happy is the man (as the Plain of Psalm 1:1 and Proverbs 8:34 for ashre; the Hebrew here has ashre). Added by Sir 13-18.
ἐπισκοπή (Sirach 16:18; 18:20)
'when he visits them' (16:18) / 'the hour of visitation' (18:20), God's coming to inspect and judge, with a gloss. Added by Sir 13-18.
godly / ungodly (as 1 Maccabees and Wisdom of Solomon for ἀσεβής) / holy (ὅσιοι 'holy sons' 39:13, 'those who are holy' 39:24); note at 37:12. Added by Sir 37-43.
γραμματεύς (Sirach 38:24)
scribe (gloss: a scholar of the Scriptures; note at 38:24 on the scribe as teacher of the law, as Ezra 7:6; topic scribes). Added by Sir 37-43.
ἰατρός / ἴασις (Sirach 10:10; 38:1–15)
doctor / healing (as Sir 07-12 at 10:10 and the Gospels' 'doctor'; Genesis 50:2 keeps 'physicians'). Added by Sir 37-43.
πεπαιδευμένος / πολύπειρος / ὑβριστής (Sirach 30-36)

well-taught (31:9; 34:19) / a man of wide experience (31:9; 36:25) / the insolent (32:23, under lead decision 13: ὕβρις 'insolence'). παιδεία follows lead decision 6 in 30-36: 'discipline' at 30:33, 34:17, 35:14; 'instruction' at 30:26 and 36:4 (note at 30:26). Added by Sir 30-36 fix.
παιδεία / ἀπαίδευτος / ὑπερηφανία / βδέλυγμα (Sirach 44-51)

under lead decisions 6 and 13: παιδεία 'instruction' throughout 44-51, where it always means teaching (44:4; 50:27; 51:16, 23, 26, 28; note at 44:4); ἀπαίδευτοι 'you who are untaught' at 51:23 (schooling); ὑπερηφανία 'pride' (48:18; 51:10); βδελύγματα 'the abhorrent things' (49:2). Added by Sir 44-51 fix.
